title: WHEN A LEADER PLEADS FOR MERCY

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Moses, "I will strike them down with a plague and destroy them, but I will make you into a nation greater and stronger than they." Moses said to the Lord, "Then the Egyptians will hear about it! By your power you brought these people up from among them. And they will tell the inhabitants of this land about it. They have already heard that you, Lord, are with these people and that you, Lord, have been seen face to face, that your cloud stays over them, and that you go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night." — Num 14:12-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God offers Moses something staggering: destroy this rebellious people and start over, making Moses himself into a great nation. It was a test of Moses' heart. Would he grasp at greatness for himself, or plead for the very people who had just tried to replace and stone his allies?

Moses does not hesitate. He begins to intercede — not for his own glory, but for God's. Watch his argument: he appeals to God's reputation among the nations. "The Egyptians will hear about it. The nations already know You are with these people." Moses' deepest concern is not himself but the honour of God's name before a watching world.

This is the mark of a true intercessor. Moses stands in the gap between a holy God and a sinful people, pleading for mercy on the basis of who God is. He could have taken the promotion. Instead he throws himself into the breach to save those who did not deserve saving. His love for the people and his jealousy for God's name are stronger than his ambition.

Here we glimpse the shadow of a greater Intercessor. Moses pleaded for a rebellious people, but Jesus does infinitely more — He does not merely argue for mercy; He purchases it with His own blood. He stands before the Father not with clever words but with His finished sacrifice. If Moses' intercession could turn away judgment, how much more secure are we in the hands of Christ, who ever lives to intercede for us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When offered personal advancement, do you seek your glory or God's?
2. Whom are you standing in the gap for in prayer right now?
3. How does it comfort you that Jesus ever lives to intercede for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me a heart like Moses that cares more for Your honour and for others than for my own advancement. Thank You for Jesus, my great Intercessor, who pleads for me with His own blood. Amen.
